sonnet.q1: It does not differ. Both get the same 401 login page showing "Invalid email or password", with the same body. The failure is recorded the same way, and timing is matched by a dummy bcrypt compare.
sonnet.q2: The email is locked (lock:<email>, 15-minute TTL). The app finds the lock before the password check and replies 429 immediately, without checking the password (bcrypt is not run). Attempts during the lock are not counted or extended.
sonnet.q3: The server always generates a new session ID and never reuses the old one. It creates the new session, then deletes the old session record, then sends the 302 to /dashboard with Set-Cookie.
sonnet.q4: Only an opaque random session ID (32 CSPRNG bytes, base64url), with no user data. The cookie is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it. It is also Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/ and host-only.
sonnet.q5: At 12 hours after login (created_at + 12 h). The 12-hour absolute cap applies even with constant activity, because each request resets the 30-minute idle clock only up to that cap.
sonnet.q6: It responds 302 to /login and clears the cookie. If the key still exists but 12 hours have passed, it also deletes the session record. An expired key reads as unknown, which is handled like missing.
sonnet.q7: The server deletes sess:hash(sid) in Redis before replying, if a cookie is present. If the session is already gone, deleting a missing key is a harmless no-op and the reply is the same: 302 to /login with the cookie cleared.
sonnet.q8: In one shared Redis instance, under key sess:<sha256(id)>. Any app instance hashes the cookie's sid and does an atomic lookup-and-extend on that key. Times come from the Redis server clock.
sonnet.q9: In Redis, in the key fail:<lowercase email>, which is a sorted set of attempt timestamps. A Lua script on each failure removes entries older than 10 minutes, adds the new one and counts the entries (the sliding window).
sonnet.q10: It compares now (Redis clock) to created_at + 12 h. If valid, it sets the key TTL to min(30 min, created_at + 12 h - now), restarting the idle clock. This is one atomic lookup-and-extend.
sonnet.q11: NOT STATED. The document covers Redis being unreachable at the lockout check, which gives a 503 before the password is checked. It does not say what happens when saving the session fails after a correct password. It only says a failure mid-way never leaves a half-logged-in state.
sonnet.q12: Redis itself removes them when the TTL lapses, through lazy deletion plus its background sweep. No cron job or cleanup code is needed.
